main_body: Green tile hip roof (rows ~4-42) over a shrine front wall with red posts, a cream shoji wall and a dark lattice door (rows 43-73), on a grey stone base
top_band: Mid column: gold finials rows 0-3, light green ridge cap rows 4-8, then green tile roof slope rows 9-42 with per-tile highlights; the lighter eave row at 41-42 forms the front edge
evidence: The roof is a large foreshortened slope seen from above, clearly separated from the vertical wall below. The red lintel beam at rows 43-46 sits directly under the eave and reads as shaded. The door lattice is darker and inset between the posts. This matches how the reference house roofs sit above their walls, so it reads as a 3/4 building rather than an elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have 5 or more green steps with per-tile highlights and dark rows, comparable to the reference tile roofs. Outlines are dark green and dark brown tinted to the adjacent material, not near-black. The door lattice, rope with paper streamers and stone base carry texture. The cream wall panels are plainer but have plaster speckle like the reference walls. Tile density is about the same as the reference.
